u0: No customer-order or slip-recovery obligation is currently pending. The agent waits for the next client or event; a new client creates an order-taking requirement, and a slip creates an immediate recovery requirement. After a completed service with no other obligations, the agent returns to this neutral condition.
u1: A client's order has been taken, but food for it has not yet been prepared. The agent still needs to obtain raw food if necessary, prepare it at the stove while the client waits, and then serve it. If the carried food slips before preparation, it must be recovered on the very next step.
u10: Two customer requirements are outstanding: an order still needs to be taken, and a taken order still needs food prepared. Both must eventually be satisfied, with service following preparation. A slip would add an urgent next-step recovery obligation.
u11: Food has just slipped while an order still needs taking and a taken order still needs food prepared. The food must be recovered on the very next step or the task fails. After recovery, both customer requirements remain, and preparing the taken order's food is still required before serving it.
u12: A taken order still needs its food prepared, and prepared food is also waiting to be served. Both requirements remain outstanding: prepare for the taken order and deliver the prepared portion. A slip would add an immediate next-step recovery requirement.
u13: Food has just slipped while a taken order still needs food prepared and prepared food still needs to be served. The food must be recovered on the very next step or the task fails. After recovery, both the preparation and service requirements remain.
u14: A mandatory next-step recovery was missed after food slipped; the agent did not have food in hand on the step after the fall. This violates the hard slip-recovery rule, and successful completion is no longer possible. The failure is irreversible.
u15: Three customer requirements are outstanding: a waiting client's order has not been taken, a taken order still needs food prepared, and prepared food still needs to be served. All must eventually be completed. No slip recovery is currently pending, but a new slip would require pickup on the very next step.
u16: Food has just slipped while a client is waiting to order, a taken order still needs food prepared, and prepared food still needs serving. The dropped food must be back in hand on the very next step or the task fails. Once recovered, all three customer requirements remain.
u2: Food for the waiting client has been prepared and is ready to serve. The remaining customer requirement is to hand the prepared food to the client. If the food slips, it must be picked up on the very next step and the service still completed.
u3: Food has just slipped and must be back in the agent's hands on the very next step. No customer-order requirement is pending in this state. Recovering the food clears the slip obligation; missing that next-step recovery causes irreversible failure.
u4: Food has just slipped while an order is already taken but not yet prepared. The agent must be holding food again on the very next step or the task fails. After recovery, the taken order still needs its food prepared and then served.
u5: Food has just slipped after preparation, while the client is still waiting to be served. The food must be recovered on the very next step or the task fails. After it is back in hand, it still has to be served to the client.
u6: A client is waiting and their order has not been taken yet. The next customer obligation is to take that order, after which food must be prepared and served. If food slips while the agent is waiting, recovering it on the following step becomes urgent.
u7: A client is waiting to have an order taken, and prepared food is also awaiting service. Both requirements remain outstanding and must eventually be completed. A slip would add an urgent requirement to recover the food on the very next step.
u8: Food has just slipped while a client is waiting whose order has not yet been taken. The food must be back in hand on the very next step or the task fails. After recovery, the client's order must still be taken and then its food prepared and served.
u9: Food has just slipped while a client is waiting to order and prepared food also needs to be served. The next-step recovery is mandatory; failing it ends the task unsuccessfully. If recovered, both the order-taking and the service obligations remain.
